competency_fulfillment.rationale: Ascending ordering is well tested -- seed 44's 6-item list '122, 131, 127, 120, 118, 132' correctly resolves to '118, 120, 122, 127, 131, 132' -- but the competency's explicit 'and vice versa' clause is never exercised in any of the 6 samples, including the new sort_order-formatted seed 50.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Every one of the 6 seeds, across both the 'ordering' formatter (42-46) and the newly sampled 'sort_order' formatter (50, '135, 122, 130, 126, 123, 125'), asks to arrange 'from smallest to largest' only; the descending-order half the competency names is completely absent.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The comma-separated number lists and consistent instruction phrasing remain readable at grade 3 quarter 1 level even at the largest list size, seed 44's 6 items.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: List length varies helpfully (3, 5, and 6 items across the seeds) and a second formatter (sort_order at seed 50) is exercised, but the direction of ordering never varies, so format diversity does not translate into task diversity.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample, including the new sort_order seed 50, is a genuine number-ordering task using values in a consistent, readable magnitude band, matching the core ordering skill this competency names.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values across all 6 seeds, including the new sort_order seed 50 (122-135), stay clustered between 115 and 135; nothing approaches even 1,000, let alone the stated 10,000 ceiling for this grade-3 quarter-1 competency.
